note: Every path here keeps the old name deliberately. `check` reports the hit count it finds under each path and refuses a path that falls below its floor, so a hand-alteration of a kept surface is reported rather than silently accepted.

kept_paths.surface: Historical evidence data and prose: landing fragments, inventory, prototype reports
kept_paths.reason: The plan requires historical evidence to keep its bytes, and the default here is to keep everything under the path: these fragments are the measured record the plan and its reviews cite, and rewriting them would restate measurements as what they were not. A new evidence file type is therefore kept without a change to this list. Only the `code` beside the data is renamed, through the excluded patterns: the Python and shell files are scripts that tests and plan gates load by path, so they follow the package. This is the split already made for docs/figures, where the rendered figure and its raw measurement JSON are kept and the script that draws it is renamed.
Plan text records the decisions and the wording in force before the cutover, including this plan, which names both names by design.
Closed sprint records describe work as it was delivered under the old name.
Research notes are historical probe records; no build or test reads them.
Archived records are history and are not read by the product.

kept_paths.surface: In-tree reckon project state, run records, reviews and crew file
kept_paths.reason: Run records and review payloads are preserved byte-for-byte here, and so are the directory name and the project key it carries. Reckon has no supported way to rename a project key, so serving the project under a new key would re-register its history under new identities. `docs/state/imas-codex` therefore keeps its name and bytes; a later migration that gives reckon a supported key rename is out of scope for this cutover.

kept_paths.surface: Reckon's typed-resource index, project-state migration record and locks
kept_paths.reason: These files name resources by their project-qualified identifiers (`imas-codex:evidence:...`, `imas-codex:plan:...`) and record where each one lives. The identifiers are keys reckon resolves against, not the product name, so the bytes stay as they are while the project keeps its key.
Crew reports are historical records of completed runs.
Tracked research probes and evaluation logs are historical records; nothing imports or executes them from the package.

kept_paths.surface: Rendered figures and their raw measurement JSON
kept_paths.reason: A rendered figure and its raw measurement JSON are evidence of the run that produced them. The figure scripts beside them are live code and are renamed.
The rename tool holds the old name as data - the replacement pattern, the kept-name list and the checks - so rewriting it would erase the mapping it exists to apply.
The tests plant an old-name reference and alter a kept-name surface to prove the checks fire; the fixtures must spell what they detect.

kept_contexts.reason: A page or figure URL mounted under the key keeps the project key: the rename tool's own report links and the evidence pages serve from /imas-codex/... because that is where reckon mounts the project, not because the product is called that. The lookbehind excludes a filesystem path (~/.local/share/imas-codex/..., /home/<user>/Code/imas-codex/...), which names the product and is renamed.

The project key passed to a reckon command names the project, not the product, and the key does not move in this cutover. `--project` passed to uv names a directory and is renamed with the checkout paths.

A project-qualified plan or resource reference names a record the live plan system resolves by key, so it is kept. Scoped to the evidence tree, where such references appear in the scripts beside the kept bytes, because outside it the same spelling is a container image tag (`ghcr.io/.../imas-codex:latest`) or an application title, both the product and both renamed.

kept_names.reason: the independently named standard-names catalog and grammar distribution keeps its name
the grammar library import names the IMAS standard names, not the product
the data-dictionary-only server keeps its imas-dd client key and kind
the data-dictionary schema file, module and accessor keep their IMAS spelling
the IMAS Python dependency is an independent scientific library
IMAS data-dictionary version settings name the IMAS dependency
DD graph labels and schema classes identify the IMAS data model
